record.paper_title: Local and Global Methods in Data Mining: Basic Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let D be a downward-closed collection of subsets of a set R. Define the positive border Bd⁺(D) to be the maximal elements of D and the negative border Bd⁻(D) to be the minimal elements of P(R) \ D. For the conjunction α = ∧_{A∈X} A, is it always true that the approximation error from truncated inclusion-exclusion satisfies e(α, D) ≤ Σ_{Y∈Bd⁺(D)} f(Y) + Σ_{Y∈Bd⁻(D)} f(Y)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11 For α = ∧A∈X A we have e(α, D) ≤ ΣY ∈Bd+(D) f(Y ) + ΣY ∈Bd−(D) f(Y ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be a finite set ("attributes" or "items"), and let $r$ be a finite collection of subsets of $R$ ("transactions"). For a subset $A \subseteq R$, define its frequency
$$f(A) = \frac{|\{t \in r : A \subseteq t\}|}{|r|}.$$
Let $\mathcal{D} \subseteq 2^R$ be a downward-closed family (i.e., if $B \in \mathcal{D}$ and $B' \subseteq B$ then $B' \in \mathcal{D}$). Define
- the positive border $\mathrm{Bd}^+(\mathcal{D})$ as the set of $\subseteq$-maximal elements of $\mathcal{D}$,
- the negative border $\mathrm{Bd}^-(\mathcal{D})$ as the set of $\subseteq$-minimal elements of $2^R \setminus \mathcal{D}$.

For a finite collection $X = \{A_1, \dots, A_n\}$ of subsets of $R$, consider the boolean conjunction $\alpha = \bigwedge_{A \in X} A$, whose true frequency is
$$f(\alpha) = \frac{|\{t \in r : A \subseteq t \text{ for all } A \in X\}|}{|r|}.$$
By the inclusion–exclusion principle,
$$f(\alpha) = \sum_{\emptyset \neq Y \subseteq X} (-1)^{|Y|+1} f\!\left(\bigcup_{A \in Y} A\right).$$
Given the downward-closed family $\mathcal{D}$, let $\widehat{f}(\alpha; \mathcal{D})$ be the truncated inclusion–exclusion estimate obtained by including only those terms $Y$ for which $\bigcup_{A \in Y} A \in \mathcal{D}$, and let
$$e(\alpha, \mathcal{D}) = \bigl| f(\alpha) - \widehat{f}(\alpha; \mathcal{D}) \bigr|$$
denote the resulting approximation error.

Prove or disprove: for every finite $R$, every transaction collection $r$, every downward-closed $\mathcal{D} \subseteq 2^R$, and every finite collection $X$ of subsets of $R$ with conjunction $\alpha = \bigwedge_{A \in X} A$,
$$e(\alpha, \mathcal{D}) \;\leq\; \sum_{Y \in \mathrm{Bd}^+(\mathcal{D})} f(Y) \;+\; \sum_{Y \in \mathrm{Bd}^-(\mathcal{D})} f(Y).$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for the "border bound conjecture" on truncated inclusion–exclusion approximation errors in terms of positive and negative borders of a downward-closed family did not surface a published proof, refutation, or partial resolution. Standard references on borders in knowledge discovery discuss the framework but do not appear to settle this specific inequality, so the status is not verifiable from public sources.

status_evidence.title: Levelwise Search and Borders of Theories in Knowledge Discovery
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational work introducing positive/negative borders of a downward-closed theory, but does not contain a proof of the conjectured truncated inclusion–exclusion bound.
status_evidence.claim: The border framework used in the conjecture is well established, but no resolution of the specific border bound inequality is recorded there.

status_evidence.title: Methods and problems in data mining (Mannila)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys open problems including bounds via borders for inclusion–exclusion approximations.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is listed among open problems with no proof provided.
